appraisal_events.evidence: l'homme que vous « adorez » ... est le plus grand imbécile que la terre ait jamais porté ... Jamais le Prince de Borodino ne recevrait chez lui ce petit bourgeois ... c'est tout de même un fameux culot de la part d'un homme dont l'arrière-grand-père était un petit fermier ... il va à peine au Jockey, tant il y est gêné, ce prétendu prince.
appraisal_events.explanation: Saint-Loup exposes the capitaine, himself the parvenu 'Prince de Borodino,' as a foolish social climber who snubs a genuinely admirable but bourgeois commandant, while his own Napoleonic-era title masks humble farming ancestry and leaves him ill at ease even at the Jockey Club.

appraisal_events.evidence: ces traits caractéristiques des Guermantes, de cette race restée si particulière au milieu du monde ... elle semble issue, aux âges de la mythologie, de l'union d'une déesse et d'un oiseau.
appraisal_events.explanation: Studying Robert's resemblance to his aunt's photograph, the narrator elevates him as visibly marked by the rare, almost mythic distinction of the Guermantes lineage.

status_effects.explanation: He is directly called the greatest fool alive and exposed as a hypocrite who despises a socially humble but admirable man despite his own recently, humbly rooted title.
His shaky footing among the old aristocracy is exposed: he is 'ni chair ni poisson' and scarcely dares appear at the Jockey Club, ill at ease among his supposed peers.
The narrator's private, admiring contemplation elevates Robert by tracing in his face the rare, almost divine distinction of the Guermantes line.
